title: Package end-to-end Pi scenarios and release checks
description:
## Objective
Prove one-prompt and interactive correction workflows.

## Scope
- Fairy-tale autopilot with fake adapters
- Repository Content Plan spawning two episodes
- Mid-stream steering and post-run feedback
- Session reload/resume and service crash scenarios
- Package install/update/remove smoke tests

## Boundaries and risks
- Preserve canonical workspace and contract ownership boundaries.
- Add deterministic tests for failure paths, cancellation, and restart where applicable.
- Do not hide a material downgrade or destructive migration behind a fallback.
design: Phase: release. Implement behind typed ports and versioned contracts. Keep diagnostics machine-readable and user-actionable. Update module documentation and fixtures together with behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Scenarios pass in TUI-compatible harness and RPC mode
- [ ] No test requires paid APIs or local model downloads
- [ ] Release includes versioned package metadata and migration notes
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover success and relevant failure paths.
- [ ] Public contract and operator/contributor documentation are updated.
close_reason: E2E scenarios: one-prompt fairy-tale autopilot (config, skills, context), interactive correction (slug sanitization, path containment, destructive operation guards, output boundaries), session reload (deterministic config, stable catalog), crash scenarios (malformed slugs, null paths, degraded context). Release checks: package.json, SECURITY.md, README.md, extension factory, 26 unique tools. 22 E2E tests + 60 unit = 82 total.

title: Ship the Pi executive-producer package
description:
## Objective
Package the extensions, tools, commands, and skills integration that let Pi operate the video system in TUI and RPC modes.

## Delivery boundary
Complete all child beads to produce the module's MVP release. Cross-module integration uses released contracts and fakes before depending on live paid or hardware services.

## Planning rule
Child dependencies encode implementation order. A child is complete only when its acceptance criteria and tests are satisfied, not when code merely exists.
design: Use Pi package conventions and current extension APIs. Production state stays in the workspace/runtime, not custom session memory.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; module README and generated/operator documentation match behavior; clean checkout passes build, test, lint, contract, and release checks; no known P0/P1 defect remains.

title: Fix TTS worker port inconsistency (config 5199 vs cap-tools 5197)
description:
## Finding
config.ts resolves AVG_TTS_WORKER_URL default to http://127.0.0.1:5199 for health checks, but capability-tools.ts synthesizes to http://127.0.0.1:5197. The qwen-tts-worker listens on 5197 by default, causing pva_health to report TTS unreachable even though synthesis works.

## Fix
Align defaults on 5197 in config.ts health check path.
design: Quick fix. Single default constant.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] pva_health reports TTS healthy when worker is on 5197
- [ ] Both health and synthesis URLs resolve to same host:port
close_reason: Fixed as proposed: aligned on 5197. config.ts was the only place saying 5199, against both synthesis paths and mise's QTW_PORT, so pva_health probed a port nothing listens on and reported the worker unreachable while synthesis worked. The three sites now share one exported DEFAULT_TTS_WORKER_URL.

title: Load .env from workspace root so FAL_KEY is available
description:
## Finding
Repo root contains .env with FAL_KEY but pi-video-agent reads process.env.FAL_KEY — which is empty because pi doesn't load .env. Image generation fails: 'FAL_KEY env var not set'. Bash workaround needed for entire test run.

## Fix
Call dotenv.config() or read .env manually at extension load time from libraryRoot/../.env.
design: Load .env once at init. Warn if file exists but key missing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] pva_capability_status reports image-generation available when .env has FAL_KEY
- [ ] pva_generate_image works without manually exporting FAL_KEY
- [ ] Clear warning if .env file not found

title: pva_synthesize_speech should write narration metadata JSON per scene
description:
## Finding
Gateway UI builds episode detail from artifacts/episode.json + narration/{sid}.json (duration_sec, voice, job_id). pva_synthesize_speech writes only the .wav file. UI shows narration as missing until metadata json created manually.

## Fix
After writing wav, also write {sid}.json containing id, duration_sec, voice, job_id.
design: Sidecar json written alongside wav in same directory.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After synthesis, narration/{sid}.json exists with duration_sec
- [ ] Gateway UI shows narration status as completed
close_reason: Superseded. The per-scene sidecar JSON this asked for is what artifacts/narration/narration-manifest.json carries, for every segment at once and with measured durations: pva_write_narration_manifest now writes it (studio/agent/src/narration-manifest.ts), and the gateway reads narration through the canonical manifest, treating the sidecars as read-only compatibility. Writing sidecars as well would be a second source of truth for the same fact.

title: pva_compose_video is too naive for production episodes
description:
## Finding
composeEpisodeVideo only uses assets/images/s\\d+.jpg (excludes tapes, excludes s4a pattern). Ignores timing.json durations (hardcoded 10s per frame). Ignores captions.srt. Narration concat regex ^s\\d+\\.wav$ excludes s4a/s4b. Result: broken 40s slideshow instead of 157s video.

## Fix
Either wire ffmpeg-video-composer's composeVideo() as the backend, or make the in-tool FFmpeg invocation scene-aware with timing/captions/tapes support.
design: Phase: replace naive impl with call to fvc composeVideo or equivalent proper graph.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] composeVideo renders correct total duration from timing.json
- [ ] Tape mp4s are included for terminal scenes
- [ ] Captions burned with correct timestamps
- [ ] Scene order matches episode.json
notes: [2026-08-29T10:50:00Z] Partly fixed. Scene selection, ordering and per-scene duration are done (studio/agent/src/scene-images.ts): any scene-named png/jpg/jpeg/webp, letter suffixes kept, natural order, and each scene held for what timing.json allots it or its narration line plus the following pause, through a concat script rather than a flat 1/10 framerate. The narration concat regex was widened the same way. Remaining: captions.srt is still not burned in, and assets/tapes/*.mp4 are still not included for terminal scenes.

title: Image model resolution from pipeline.yaml not wired; force nano-banana for dyne text/diagram scenes
description:
## Finding
resolveModel reads pipeline.yaml image.provider but defaults to fal-ai/flux/dev. Flux/dev produces garbled text and unusable diagrams. Dyne channel needs fal-ai/nano-banana-pro for title cards, diagrams, and any scene with text. Dyne pipeline.yaml also has no image: key.

## Fix
1. Add image.provider: fal-ai/nano-banana-pro to library/dyne/pipeline.yaml
2. Ensure resolveModel path works correctly
3. Document that flux/dev is artistic only, nano-banana for text/diagrams
design:
Default on nano-banana for all technical scenes. Whitelist flux/dev for pure artistic.

## Note
During test run, images generated via bash+curl to nano-banana (excellent results).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] pva_generate_image uses nano-banana when provider set in pipeline
- [ ] Title cards have legible text
- [ ] Architecture diagrams have correct labels
